notes.title: The Species update
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42837783/59c880f61d855302aad4419d16341a60f5e0b285.png[/img]
Among many small improvements, this update brings a global update to all the playable species of the game. 

[h2]Species traits[/h2]

Here is what the different species now do in the game:
- Humans now have a bonus in ship weapon proficiency, at the helm and a very slight bonus in saber proficiency.
- Orcs are now red/orange skinned, to be more consistent with their affinity with fire and to make them more recognizable from trolls. In addition to high fire resistance, they also put out fires more quickly.
- Trolls are now green, with slightly improved natural regeneration of their hit points. This is faster if they are idle.
- Eladrins have a very useful magic shield, but are rather fragile, slow and weaker in melee. They improve the charge speed of the arcane tower.
- Elves are formidable hand-to-hand combatants: not only do they inflict far more damage, but they also have the unique ability to dodge attacks. They also grant a speed bonus to birds when managing the perch.
- Dwarves repair everything much faster, and are experts at handling overdrive, engine and barricade repair.
- Hiring prices, health points and speed of all species have also been adjusted.

[h2]Other updates[/h2]

🌟 New:
- The rework and balance of the playable species of the game is complete.
- Some enemies can now try out a new strategy and change it if things don't go their way.
- Two new music tracks have also been released in this update, ahead of the planned music update. 🎵

⚖ Balance:
- Increase Eladrin shield generation time from 5s to 6s
- Reduce Greek fire ignite chance from 65% to 60% and increase reload time from 9s to 10s

🎆 Graphic:
- new key art & Steam capsule.
- improved UI and game scaling to fit all the common screen resolutions and ratios.
- Added Proportional zoom option (experimental): for less common screen resolutions this can be used to make the ships fit better in the screen (at the cost of less sharp sprites).

💻 UI / Quality of life:
- Changed shop tabs colour to make it more visible that you can also upgrade and sell equipment in some shops.
- show current ship weapons when on the “buy weapon” tab of a shop
- show available room slots when on the “buy room” tab of a shop

The update is now live in the demo!

notes.title: The ships update is live
notes.content:
After months of work, I'm pleased to present the most important graphical update to Reclaim the Sea since the first demo. This update focuses primarily on the addition of new ships. The game now features several dozen visually different ships, to offer more visual variety in encounters and to reinforce the personality of the different factions present in the game.

Here are just a few of the ships you'll be able to play or encounter in Reclaim The Sea :
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42837783/2d934f2d9c857a28a59935fa99b4443617502405.jpg[/img]

This update also brings a few other graphical enhancements, such as trail and splash effects, new graphics and animations for mechanical birds, new skin colors for some playable species, and small interface improvements.

A new ship is also unlockable and playable in the demo: The Gearwright. Thanks to its large platforms, this ship allows for the installation of numerous rooms, at the expense of pure firepower. Test it out and let me know what you think!

This update is an opportunity to update the game's roadmap from now until release:
https://steamcommunity.com/games/2096860/announcements/detail/4137190132774198527
In addition to the species overhaul, which is well underway, many other new features are in the pipeline, but I can't tell you more about them just yet!

- A new ship is also unlockable and playable in the demo: The Gearwright.

⚡ change inspired by the community & content creators


[h2]Fire rework[/h2]
Before this update, fire was an all-or-nothing strategy: small amounts of fire were almost useless, and large amounts became impossible to counter. This update makes several changes to the way fire works to improve the balance.

- Now, each fire slowly produces damage to the ship's hull and possibly to the room in which it is located, depending on its power.
- Propagation has also been modified: each fire gradually gains in power. When it reaches a certain power, it spreads the fire to a surrounding tile.
- Conversely, fighting a fire will gradually reduce its power.

notes.title: Boarding update
notes.content:
Hi everyone,

I'm super excited to announce that the "boarding and combat" update is now complete and available in the demo. This is without a doubt the most important update to the game since the launch of the demo.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42837783/b134df49aee610932c95257dd3f6ee9d5c6c70df.png[/img]

It was by far THE most requested feature by all players who tried out the demo: the ability to engage in sword fights between crews. After testing a number of solutions, I opted for the creation of a grappling room, enabling crew members to be sent and repatriated at close range. (Another solution I'm considering looks interesting, so I'll keep it in mind for a future update.)

The addition of melee combat required a lot of changes under the hood, notably to the 3 artificial intelligence systems of the game (general, enemy and enemy ship), so I hope no bugs have crept into this update. If you notice any, please feel free to report them via the in-game bug-reporting tool.

This update also includes new boarding-related content and the usual array of improvements and fixes, detailed below.

🌟 New:
- New room: 2x2 grappling room
- Fighting: crew member will now attack any enemy crew member on adjacent tile
- New fighting skill: dealing damage in close combat give fighting skill experience
- New events related to boarding

⚖ Balance:
- Adjusted infirmary heal speed

🎆 Graphic:
- Added room border to enemy rooms.
- New icon for hull upgrade, to differentiate it from other ship augments.

🐞 Bugfix:
- Fixed a bug where you could not click on your destination on the map if it was too close to the interruption point.
- Fixed a bug where infirmary would heal 2x too fast under certain conditions
- Fixed missing end of game stats / restart screen on defeat

💻 UI:
- Allow any character in crew member rename field (including numbers) ⚡
- Display ship weapon information on the room tooltip ⚡
- Display destination information directly on the room tooltip ⚡

⚡ change inspired by the community & content creators

notes.title: Update 0.8.0.7 : The French update
notes.content:
Hello pirates!

A new update is now available. It adds some fixes and improvements (see below), but the main feature is the ability to switch the game to French.

My goal is to translate Reclaim the Sea into as many languages as possible, and French served as a test for different translation solutions. Why French first? The first reason is that French is the second language after English in wishlists. The second is that, as I speak French myself, it allowed me to rigorously control the quality of the translation, which I wouldn't be able to do in other languages. I tested different automatic translation solutions: Google, DeepL, ChatGPT. Even though these solutions generally help understand the idea and save time on translation, the result is far from being of an acceptable quality level, and there are often misunderstandings or completely incomprehensible sentences. Translations in other languages will therefore be done by humans!

Feel free to add the game to your wishlist and talk about it if you want the game to be translated into your language.

notes.title: Update 0.7.2.0 : bufixes and clarification
notes.content:
After the previous hot-fix update, this update fixes less critical bugs and improves the clarity of some aspect of the game with new tips and descriptions.

The reworked map generation algorithm will allow you discover more various events while playing the demo. 

🌟 New:
Added more attack options in some non-hostile events.
Reworked map generation algorithm to increase event diversity.
Changed random character name selection to avoid duplicate names.

🐞 Bugfix:
- Fixed a bug when the demo final event would not trigger 50% of the time
- Fixed a bug where the Travel button was sometimes transparent

notes.title: Ammo update
notes.content:
Hi fellow sailors,

Previous play tests have shown that the long range weapon combined with defensive equipment tends to be the most effective strategy. And I obviously want several strategies to be viables.
Before the update, by staying at long range, you use the increased miss rate of your opponent to help your defense systems to recharge. It also gives you more time to deal with fire in case of incendiary weapons. And, icing on the cake, longer fights give more experience to your manning crew. Of course, you have to be able to maintain that long distance with the enemy ship. But still, this strategy had too many pros and too few cons.

So, here comes the “Ammo Update” which introduces… ammo! (you guessed it?). This new resource is consumed every time a ship weapons shoots. Ammo is not very expensive, but on the long run, always staying at long range will impact your economy. It also encourages you to go the more often more risky close distance. 

The ammo update also solves a problematic situation that could happen since the first versions of the game: in some rare cases, you had no way to win the fight (due to inappropriate weapons or enemy heavy defenses), but you also had no way to flee, due to enemy superior speed. Now that the enemy also has limited ammo, the fight will always end.

The ammo update also comes with new events related to … ammo. Like trading ammo, using ammo, etc.

This update also comes with many small new features, balance changes (most of them making the game a little easier) and bug fixes. Most notably, all text events now have proper texts. No more only “you find an enemy ship”. You will be able to learn a little more about the various factions of the game.

notes.title: Room damage update
notes.content:
Since the first versions of the game I always felt that the Reclaim the Sea was missing ways of disturbing your enemy, and also in return things that could mess with your plan in a combat. Many feedbacks from the demo have confirmed this. There were already several mechanics like fire or holes, or the fight for the distance between ships. And they have been rebalanced many times since the first version, but now I have added a direct way of denying the enemy the use of one its room: to damage it!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42837783/a15df561ffe35f0deb1f15451f21d3e956acf4a2.png[/img]

Rooms now have health points and take damage when taking hits, thus reducing their efficiency or completely shutting them down on low HP. All existing weapons have been updated to offer some room damage, some more than others. This new mechanic also opens new fight strategies and new weapons possibilities.

And speaking of weapons, the Thunder mortar is the first weapon specially designed to damage enemy ship rooms. In a few shots it will shut them down, but in return it does not inflict any damage to the ship hull.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42837783/c6d35d0046073b64c1454e9a0e9d56ffa22eface.gif[/img]

notes.title: Automaton update is live
notes.content:
How to handle all the tasks on your ship without hiring many crew members (and feeding them) ?

[b]The answer is technology of course![/b]

With the new automatons center, you can let automatons take care of all the little tasks on the ship, like loading weapons, piloting, repairing, etc.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42837783/7e0caf9163be377ace07da59984fe9f5e959de05.gif[/img]

They are not as efficient as living crew members and don’t gain experience, but with some investment in upgrades, they can almost catch up rookie crew members. And they still don’t use any food, thus nice savings in sight!

The automaton update is now complete, and also includes a new ship : the automaton ship, and a new weapon : the falconet, a fast firing light cannon.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42837783/3e5c5d8e302385ed0d90144d380b5c422f4fa8b2.png[/img]
